text:
hana: Heads-up from model onboarding: Kibou v0.8-int6 (cascade quant profile) failed locale-mix-v3 smoke. Mixed CJK+Hebrew testcases show token-splitting and mirrored double quotes. sacreBLEU down ~3.6 vs fp32 baseline.

raj: ouch. can you paste a minimal repro?

hana: yes. used locale-mix-v3 case id hebrew_cjk_quotes_01. payload I POSTed: 
```json
{
  \"src\": \"他说: \u05d0\u05d1\u05d2 \"hello\"\",
  \"lang\": \"zh-he_mixed\"
}
```
Output (raw UTF-8 shown): 
```
\u8bf7\u8bb0: \u200f\u05d0\u05d1\u05d2 \uff02hello\uff02
```
Note leading RLM (U+200F) before hebrew and FULLWIDTH QUOTATION MARKS inserted around english hello. The fp32 baseline returns: 
```
他说:  hello
```
(meaning regular ASCII quotes and no RLM).

mei: weird. did tokenization boundaries change in quantized vocab mapping?

hana: token dump from kibou-int6: 
```
TOKENS: [\"\u8bf7\u8bb0\", \":\", \"\u200f\", \"\u05d0\", \"\u05d1\", \"\u05d2\", \"\uff02\", \"hello\", \"\uff02\"]
```
whereas fp32 token dump: 
```
TOKENS: [\"\u8bf7\u8bb0\", \":\", \"\u05d0\", \"\u05d1\", \"\u05d2\", \"\\\"\", \"hello\", \"\\\"\"]
```
So kibou-int6 inserted U+200F and used FULLWIDTH_QUOTE (U+FF02) tokens.

raj: that RLM looks like a bidi marker; why would quant path insert it? did we run shaping in post-detok?

mei: check the quant conversion mapping script. we had a replacement rule that maps unknown control bytes to 0xFFFD during qpack. Maybe some multi-byte sequence was treated as control and replaced with U+200F during a cleanup pass. Also note the fullwidth-quote replacement probably from our \"east-asian-normalize\" fastpath in runtime.

hana: added raw byte dump from tokenizer stage (kibou-int6 job artifact): 
```
BYTES: [E8 AF B7, E8 AE A0, 3A, EF BB BF, D7 90, D7 91, D7 92, EF BC 82, 68 65 6C 6C 6F, EF BC 82]
```
See EF BB BF (BOM) appearing right before hebrew bytes in quant path. fp32 bytes didn't have BOM.

raj: BOM sneaking in explains some of the replacements. Where would a BOM be introduced? maybe our quant packing step wrote a UTF-8-BOM during join of segments. There's a qpack helper that concatenates locale snippets; a mistaken flag might be setting write_bom=true for some codepaths.

mei: confirmed: conversion script qpack.py line 421 had a write_text(open_mode='wb', add_bom=env.FLAG_ADD_BOM) that defaulted to true in CI for int6 builds due to an env var not set. fp32 build did not set that flag.

hana: nice catch. can we hotfix CI/env to unset BOM and re-run onboarding?

ops-bot: CI run requested: ci/kibou-int6/onboard -> patch/remove-bom-env by raj. ETA 8m.

mei: also adding defensive step: runtime fastpath that normalizes east-asian punctuation should skip when previous script is non-east-asian (is_cjk(prev)==false). That will avoid converting ASCII quotes to fullwidth when preceding script is Hebrew or Latin.

raj: pushing env fix and runtime guard. adding unit test mixing CJK+Hebrew+ASCII quotes.

ci-bot: patch pushed, running locale-mix-v3 smoke. artifacts will appear in ~10m.

(hana): re-run locally after changes: kibou-int6 now returns tokens: [\"\u8bf7\u8bb0\", \":\", \"\u05d0\", \"\u05d1\", \"\u05d2\", \"\\\"\", \"hello\", \"\\\"\"] and output string: 
```
他说: אבג \"hello\"
```
BLEU delta vs fp32 now -0.2 (within noise).

mei: good. follow-ups:
- add locale-mix-v3 hebrew_cjk_quotes_01 to onboarding gate for all quant profiles
- update qpack.py to default add_bom=false and add unit test for write_bom flag
- add runtime guard skip-east-asian-normalize-if-prev-not-cjk

raj: i'll file a brief onboarding note in the model bring-up doc explaining this BOM-env pitfall and the mitigation.

hana: thanks team. leaving thread open until nightly passes. small perf note: the runtime guard adds ~0.3% p50 but worth it.

ci-bot: nightly locale-mix-v3 job enqueued.

mei: once nightly green we should backport to recent int6/int8 candidate branches.

raj: will schedule backports. :white_check_mark:
